# Automated Filling Line Control

- **Difficulty:** Easy (easy)

## Requirements

An automated filling line responsible for cleaning, filling, capping, and packaging bottles. Each step of the production line is controlled by PLC and triggered by signals from sensors and operators.
Control requirements:
When the sensor bottleSensor detects a bottle, it triggers the start of the cleaning pump and continues to work.
After cleaning is completed, the operator operates the button cleaningConfirmButton to trigger the cleaning completion signal, automatically starting the filling valve for filling.
After filling is completed, the operator operates the button fillingConfirmButton to trigger the filling completion signal, automatically starting the capping machine for capping.
After capping is completed, the operator operates the button cappingConfirmButton to trigger the capping completion signal, starting the packing machine for packaging.
After packaging is completed, the operator operates the button packingConfirmButton to trigger the packaging completion signal, lighting up the packaging completion indicator light.
After the operator picks up the packaged bottle, they press the confirmation button finishedButton to reset the indicator light and prepare for the next bottle's production cycle.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `bottleSensor` | `BOOL` | The bottle reaches the sensor, triggering a signal when a bottle is detected |
| Input | `cleaningConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the cleaning process |
| Input | `fillingConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the filling process |
| Input | `cappingConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the capping process |
| Input | `packingConfirmButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm the completion of the packaging process |
| Input | `finishedButton` | `BOOL` | Operator confirmation button, used to confirm that the bottle has been picked up |
| Output | `Pump_Motor` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the cleaning pump motor |
| Output | `Filling_Valve` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the filling valve |
| Output | `Capping_Machine` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the capping machine |
| Output | `Packing_Machine` | `BOOL` | Control output for the operation of the packing machine |
| Output | `Completion_Light` | `BOOL` | Indicator light for packaging completion |

## Q01 灌装线

观察器按输入维护独立阶段：idle→clean→fill→cap→pack→done→idle。idle仅由bottleSensor启动；clean/fill/cap/pack分别由对应ConfirmButton推进；done仅由finishedButton复位。阶段错误的确认按钮不推进。阶段输出依次为Pump_Motor、Filling_Valve、Capping_Machine、Packing_Machine、Completion_Light。`stageOutputOK`表示对应阶段输出有效且其他阶段输出关闭，这是当前有限测试采用的顺序工序解释。

```text
G(idleBefore & bottleSensor -> R1(cleanOutputOK))
G(cleanBefore & cleaningConfirmButton -> R1(fillOutputOK))
G(fillBefore & fillingConfirmButton -> R1(capOutputOK))
G(capBefore & cappingConfirmButton -> R1(packOutputOK))
G(packBefore & packingConfirmButton -> R1(doneOutputOK))
G(doneBefore & finishedButton -> R1(idleOutputOK))
G(waitingForCurrentConfirmation -> currentStageHeld)
G(wrongStageConfirmationOnly -> observerStageUnchanged)
```

# Dual-Word Edge Detection

- **Difficulty:** Easy (easy)

## Requirements

Write a function block FB that checks for rising and falling edges in each bit of a dual-word (DWord) input value every cycle. The function block should be able to detect and report changes, rising edges, and falling edges in the input value.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `value` | `DWORD` | The input value to be checked for changes and edge triggering |
| Output | `hasChanged` | `BOOL` | True indicates that the input value has changed |
| Output | `hasRisingEdges` | `BOOL` | True indicates that rising edges have occurred in the input value |
| Output | `risingBits` | `DWORD` | The bit stream of rising edges, where each bit indicates whether the corresponding input bit has experienced a rising edge (1 for a rising edge, 0 for no rising edge) |
| Output | `noOfRisingBits` | `USINT` | The number of rising edges in the input value |
| Output | `hasFallingEdges` | `BOOL` | True indicates that falling edges have occurred in the input value |
| Output | `fallingBits` | `DWORD` | The bit stream of falling edges, where each bit indicates whether the corresponding input bit has experienced a falling edge (1 for a falling edge, 0 for no falling edge) |
| Output | `noOfFallingBits` | `USINT` | The number of falling edges in the input value |

ltl.title: Q02 DWORD边沿检测
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q02 DWORD边沿检测

跳过第一次调用的历史初始化差异。从第二次调用起，独立保存`prevValue`：`rising=value & ~prevValue & 0xFFFFFFFF`，`falling=prevValue & ~value & 0xFFFFFFFF`；popcount为32位中1的个数。

```text
G(historyReady -> risingBitsOK)
G(historyReady -> fallingBitsOK)
G(historyReady -> risingCountOK)
G(historyReady -> fallingCountOK)
G(historyReady -> changedFlagOK)
G(historyReady -> risingFlagOK)
G(historyReady -> fallingFlagOK)
```

命题分别定义为`risingBits=rising`、`fallingBits=falling`、`noOfRisingBits=popcount(rising)`、`noOfFallingBits=popcount(falling)`、`hasChanged=(value!=prevValue)`、`hasRisingEdges=(rising!=0)`、`hasFallingEdges=(falling!=0)`。

# Alarm Handling - **Difficulty:** Easy (easy) ## Requirements In industrial automation systems, monitoring the status of equipment is crucial. When equipment parameters exceed the normal range, the system needs to issue an alarm. To avoid frequent triggering of alarms due to minor fluctuations in parameters, an alarm management system with hysteresis function needs to be implemented. When Value is greater than hiLevel, trigger high alarm hiAlarm. When Value is less than hiLevel-hystWindow, exit high alarm hiAlarm. When Value is less than loLevel, trigger low alarm loAlarm. When Value is greater than loLevel+hystWindow, exit low alarm loAlarm. If loLevel is greater than or equal to hiLevel, output error error=true, status=16#8001, and exit the program If the hysteresis window value hystWindow is greater than or equal to the deviation range between hiLevel and loLevel, output error error=true, status=16#8002 ## Interface Definition | Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Input | `Value` | `REAL` | Input value | | Input | `hiLevel` | `REAL` | High limit alarm value | | Input | `loLevel` | `REAL` | Low limit alarm value | | Input | `hystWindow` | `REAL` | Hysteresis window | | Output | `hiAlarm` | `BOOL` | High limit alarm | | Output | `loAlarm` | `BOOL` | Low limit alarm | | Output | `error` | `BOOL` | FALSE: No error occurred;
TRUE: Error occurred during execution of FB | | Output | `status` | `WORD` | Status code |

ltl.title: Q03 滞环报警
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q03 滞环报警

`invalidLimits`为loLevel>=hiLevel；`invalidWindow`为hystWindow>=hiLevel-loLevel且非invalidLimits；`valid`为两者均否。`highSet/Reset`分别为Value>hiLevel、Value<hiLevel-hystWindow；低报警相反，严格比较；边界相等保持上一报警状态。无效配置时的报警输出是否清零，题面没有统一规定，不作为规约必须项。

```text
G(invalidLimits -> error8001)
G(invalidWindow -> error8002)
G(valid -> normalStatus)
G(valid & highSet -> hiAlarm)
G(valid & highReset -> !hiAlarm)
G(valid & highBand -> highAlarmHeld)
G(valid & lowSet -> loAlarm)
G(valid & lowReset -> !loAlarm)
G(valid & lowBand -> lowAlarmHeld)
```

`error8001/8002`包含error=TRUE及相应status；normalStatus表示error=FALSE、status=0。highBand/lowBand为既不触发也不复位的区间；Held表示post报警等于pre报警。负滞环的额外处置不打分。

# Jam Pump Debouncing and Runtime Maintenance

- **Difficulty:** Easy (easy)

## Requirements

Control a jam transfer pump on a food production line, including viscosity-signal debouncing, emergency-stop priority, runtime accumulation and a maintenance-due indication.

1. Accept the viscosity condition only after VISCOSITY_OK has remained TRUE for DebounceTime. Invalidate the condition immediately when the input becomes FALSE.
2. Allow VFD_RUN to be TRUE only when PASTE_E_STOP_NC is TRUE and the viscosity condition is valid. An emergency stop immediately disables the run output and clears any incomplete debounce timing.
3. Accumulate PUMP_RUNTIME_ACC using the actual invocation interval CycleTime only while VFD_RUN is TRUE. Preserve the accumulated time while the pump is stopped.
4. Set PUMP_MAINT_DUE when accumulated runtime reaches 500 hours. This indication is informational and must not affect pump operation or the safety permissive.
5. At power-up, initialize the run output to OFF, accumulated runtime to zero and the maintenance indication to FALSE.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `VISCOSITY_OK` | `BOOL` | Raw signal indicating that viscosity is within the permitted range. |
| Input | `PASTE_E_STOP_NC` | `BOOL` | Normally closed emergency-stop circuit; TRUE permits operation and FALSE means emergency stop. |
| Input | `DebounceTime` | `TIME` | Required continuous valid duration for the viscosity signal; must be positive. |
| Input | `CycleTime` | `TIME` | Actual elapsed interval represented by this invocation; must be positive. |
| Output | `VFD_RUN` | `BOOL` | Pump variable-frequency-drive run command. |
| Output | `PUMP_MAINT_DUE` | `BOOL` | Maintenance indication when accumulated runtime reaches 500 hours. |
| Output | `PUMP_RUNTIME_ACC` | `LTIME` | Accumulated enabled runtime, using a long-duration time type. |

ltl.title: Q04 黏度泵、消抖及维护
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q04 黏度泵、消抖及维护

v3采样约定：CycleTime等于距离上一实际调用的间隔，首拍为0ms；固定扫描不再跳过中间时间却只累计一拍。

`permissive=VISCOSITY_OK & PASTE_E_STOP_NC`；`debounced`由独立连续有效时钟计算，首次有效时elapsed=0，elapsed>=DebounceTime时有效。当前有限测试采用急停恢复后重新确认的解释。`runtimeOK`表示本拍运行时post累计=pre累计+CycleTime，停机时保持；时间统一换算到相同单位。`maintenanceOK`表示PUMP_MAINT_DUE与累计>=500小时等价。

```text
G(initial -> pumpInitialOK)
G(!PASTE_E_STOP_NC -> !VFD_RUN)
G(!VISCOSITY_OK -> !VFD_RUN)
G(VFD_RUN -> debounced)
G(permissive & debounced -> VFD_RUN)
G(runtimeOK)
G(maintenanceOK)
```

pumpInitialOK为运行关闭、累计0、维护FALSE。维护到期不加入运行许可。已完成消抖后发生急停的恢复策略在题面中有解释空间；若采用不同契约，应作为协议变更而非直接修改历史分数。


协议待确认项：原题规定CycleTime为正，迭代分支首拍使用0表示尚无调用间隔；本导出保留原判据并显式标记，不修改原题。500小时=1,800,000,000ms，超出通用task_spec的1e9时间戳上限，应使用专用时间适配器。

# Weld Gap Alarm and Startup Inhibition

- **Difficulty:** Easy (easy)

## Requirements

Control a weld-gap alarm with power-up monitoring inhibition, input debouncing during normal monitoring and emergency-stop priority.

1. Gap_Exceeded indicates that the scanner has detected a weld gap exceeding the permitted 1.5 mm value.
2. Begin with a 5-second initialization inhibition period after power-up. During this period, Operator_Alert is FALSE, Weld_Soft_Start_Active is TRUE, and gap-signal debounce time does not accumulate.
3. Resume gap monitoring after initialization. Allow the alarm only after Gap_Exceeded has remained TRUE for DebounceTime. When the signal becomes FALSE, switch off the alarm and clear debounce timing.
4. When Weld_E_Stop_NC is FALSE, the emergency stop takes priority over initialization and normal monitoring. Operator_Alert must immediately become FALSE and any incomplete debounce timing must be cleared.
5. Weld_Soft_Start_Active indicates only the power-up inhibition period; it does not represent a continuous speed ramp.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `Gap_Exceeded` | `BOOL` | Scanner indication that the gap exceeds 1.5 mm. |
| Input | `Weld_E_Stop_NC` | `BOOL` | TRUE means the emergency stop is inactive; FALSE means it is active. |
| Input | `DebounceTime` | `TIME` | Gap-signal debounce duration during normal monitoring; must be positive. |
| Output | `Operator_Alert` | `BOOL` | Audible and visual alarm command. |
| Output | `Weld_Soft_Start_Active` | `BOOL` | Monitoring-inhibition status during the 5-second power-up initialization. |

ltl.title: Q05 焊缝报警与启动抑制
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q05 焊缝报警与启动抑制

`initializing`为上电后不足5000ms。独立消抖仅在初始化结束且Weld_E_Stop_NC、Gap_Exceeded均真时累计；初始化内或条件失效立即清零。`gapReady`表示消抖达到DebounceTime。

```text
G(initializing -> !Operator_Alert)
G(initializing -> Weld_Soft_Start_Active)
G(!initializing -> !Weld_Soft_Start_Active)
G(!Weld_E_Stop_NC -> !Operator_Alert)
G(!Gap_Exceeded -> !Operator_Alert)
G(!initializing & Weld_E_Stop_NC & gapReady -> Operator_Alert)
G(Operator_Alert -> !initializing & Weld_E_Stop_NC & gapReady)
```

Weld_Soft_Start_Active只表示启动抑制，不解释为连续调速斜坡；急停不产生额外的报警。

# Aeration Blower Delayed Start

- **Difficulty:** Easy (easy)

## Requirements

Control a wastewater-treatment aeration blower with a low-dissolved-oxygen demand, a 5-second start delay, emergency-stop priority and start-cycle counting.

1. Start delay timing when both DO_LOW and AERATION_E_STOP_NC are TRUE. Allow BLOWER_RUN to become TRUE only after these conditions have remained satisfied for 5 seconds.
2. If DO_LOW becomes FALSE or an emergency stop occurs, immediately disable BLOWER_RUN and reset the start timer, whether timing is incomplete or complete. A new demand must wait the full 5 seconds again.
3. Increment AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT once on each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of BLOWER_RUN. Do not count repeatedly during continuous operation.
4. At power-up, initialize the blower to OFF and the start count to zero. The start delay gates a BOOL enable; no continuous speed ramp is required.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `DO_LOW` | `BOOL` | Dissolved oxygen is below its threshold and aeration is needed. |
| Input | `AERATION_E_STOP_NC` | `BOOL` | TRUE means the emergency stop is inactive; FALSE means it is active. |
| Output | `BLOWER_RUN` | `BOOL` | Blower motor-contactor run command. |
| Output | `AERATION_BLOWER_CYCLE_COUNT` | `UINT` | Count of actual blower starts. |

ltl.title: Q06 曝气风机
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q06 曝气风机

`eligible=DO_LOW & AERATION_E_STOP_NC`；`delayReady`为自本轮连续eligible首次调用起elapsed>=5000ms。任何eligible失效都会清除观察器时钟。`startCountOK`表示运行输出每次FALSE→TRUE时计数加1，其余保持；有限测试不外推溢出策略。

```text
G(initial -> blowerInitialOK)
G(!eligible -> !BLOWER_RUN)
G(BLOWER_RUN -> eligible & delayReady)
G(eligible & delayReady -> BLOWER_RUN)
G(startCountOK)
```

blowerInitialOK为运行FALSE、计数0。开始计时的首拍elapsed=0，不把某次调用前的未知时间算进等待。

ltl.title: Q07 五泵切换
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q07 五泵切换

```text
G(!mode & enabled -> manualSelectionOK)
G(mode & enabled -> topThreeOK)
G(configPreserved)
```

# Analog Batch Processing

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

Write a PLC function block that processes analog inputs in batches and converts them into engineering values.

1. analogValues supplies the raw-value array. channels supplies per-channel settings and receives conversion results. count specifies how many channels to process from the beginning of the arrays. The caller must provide count from zero through the smaller of the two array lengths. Match channels by ordinal position starting at each array's own lower bound. Read analogValues without modifying it.
2. Each channel is enabled by its enable field and converted according to measuringMode. Read configuration fields without modifying them; write only retVal and outputValue.
3. For measuringMode 0, perform non-temperature linear scaling: when bipolar is FALSE, map raw values 0..27648 to loLIM..hiLIM; when TRUE, map -27648..27648 to loLIM..hiLIM.
4. For measuringMode 1, perform standard-temperature conversion: outputValue is one tenth of the raw analog value.
5. For measuringMode 2, perform climatic-temperature conversion: outputValue is one hundredth of the raw analog value.
6. If measuringMode is not 0, 1 or 2, set that channel's retVal to 16#8001 and skip its conversion.
7. If hiLIM is less than or equal to loLIM, set that channel's retVal to 16#8002 and skip its conversion.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `count` | `DINT` | Number of channels to be converted |
| Input/Output | `analogValues` | `ARRAY[*] OF INT` | Variable-length analog array passed by reference to preserve its bounds. Read-only to the function block; no element may be modified. |
| Input/Output | `channels` | `ARRAY[*] OF ST_AnalogChannel` | Channel records passed by reference. Configuration fields are read-only; write only retVal and outputValue. |
| Input field | `channels[].enable` | `BOOL` | Channel conversion enable. Read-only to the function block. |
| Input field | `channels[].hiLIM` | `REAL` | Upper engineering-unit limit. Read-only to the function block. |
| Input field | `channels[].loLIM` | `REAL` | Lower engineering-unit limit. Read-only to the function block. |
| Input field | `channels[].bipolar` | `BOOL` | FALSE selects unipolar and TRUE selects bipolar operation. Read-only to the function block. |
| Input field | `channels[].measuringMode` | `INT` | 0 non-temperature, 1 standard temperature, 2 climatic temperature. Read-only to the function block. |
| Output field | `channels[].retVal` | `WORD` | Per-channel status code written by the function block. |
| Output field | `channels[].outputValue` | `REAL` | Converted value written by the function block. |

Rows named `channels[].fieldName` describe the element fields of ST_AnalogChannel, rather than additional function-block parameters.

ltl.title: Q08 模拟量批处理
ltl.definitions_and_rules_markdown:
## Q08 模拟量批处理

调用方保证0<=count<=两个数组长度的较小值。第k个元素配对各自lowerBound+k。FB只能写被处理通道的retVal/outputValue；原始值、配置、未处理通道保持。禁用通道不执行转换。

```text
G(rawArrayPreserved)
G(channelConfigPreserved)
G(unprocessedChannelsPreserved)
G(enabledInvalidMode -> channelError8001)
G(enabledInvalidLimits -> channelError8002)
G(enabledValidMode0 -> linearScalingOK)
G(enabledValidMode1 -> standardTemperatureOK)
G(enabledValidMode2 -> climaticTemperatureOK)
```

对所有处理通道逐项展开：单极性缩放loLIM+raw*(hiLIM-loLIM)/27648；双极性为loLIM+(raw+27648)*(hiLIM-loLIM)/55296；温度分别raw/10、raw/100。模式不在0/1/2时报8001，hiLIM<=loLIM时报8002。两种错误同时发生时的优先级、禁用时输出值和超量程钳位未由题面完整规定，应单列假设，不能无条件作为模型缺陷。

# Calculate Moving Average

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

Write a function block FB that calculates and updates a moving arithmetic mean. The moving arithmetic mean is a method of averaging over consecutive data points, where each new data point replaces the oldest data point, and then the average is recalculated.

1. When cyclicExecution is TRUE, a new data value is automatically read and the moving average average is updated every scan cycle.
2. Provide an external trigger signal trigger, which reads a new data value and updates the moving average upon each rising edge.
3. Provide a reset function reset, which resets the moving average calculation when the reset signal is TRUE. If the window size is less than 1 or greater than 100, output an error status and status code.

The status parameter indicates the execution status of the program:
- 16#0000: Execution successful
- 16#8200: Window length setting error, please set a value between 1 and 100.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `cyclicExecution` | `BOOL` | When TRUE, periodic reading is performed, and trigger has no effect |
| Input | `trigger` | `BOOL` | External trigger signal, reads value upon each rising edge |
| Input | `value` | `LREAL` | Newly read data value |
| Input | `windowSize` | `INT` | The window size for the moving average, which must be between 1 and 100 |
| Input | `reset` | `BOOL` | Reset signal, resets the moving average calculation when TRUE |
| Output | `average` | `LREAL` | The moving average |
| Output | `windowSizeReached` | `BOOL` | FALSE: Maximum window width not yet reached TRUE: Maximum window width has been reached |
| Output | `error` | `BOOL` | FALSE: No error occurred TRUE: An error occurred during the execution of FB |
| Output | `status` | `WORD` | Status code |

ltl.title: Q09 移动平均

## Q09 移动平均

A simple automated production line consists of three workstations: Workstation A, Workstation B, and Workstation C. # Slab Thickness Alarm and Fault History

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

Monitor slab-thickness faults on a stone-cutting line, including minimum alarm holding, fault counting, normal-cutting runtime accumulation and a history of the five most recent faults.

1. When THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is TRUE, THICKNESS_FAULT indicates that thickness deviation exceeds tolerance. Activate THICKNESS_ALARM immediately when the fault becomes TRUE, and hold each triggered alarm for at least 500 ms. Keep the alarm active while the fault persists.
2. On each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of a valid fault signal, increment Slab_Fault_Counter and store the current FaultTimestamp in element 0 of Slab_Fault_History. Shift older entries toward higher indices, retaining only the five most recent entries.
3. Accumulate Slab_Runtime_Accumulator using CycleTime only while CUTTING_RUN is TRUE, the thickness signal is valid and no thickness fault is present. Otherwise preserve the accumulated value.
4. At power-up or whenever THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is FALSE, switch off the alarm and clear its holding state. Do not add fault records or accumulate normal runtime while the signal is invalid.
5. At power-up, initialize the fault count, accumulated runtime and all five history entries to zero. Statistics and history are for observation and maintenance only; they must not alter the cutting equipment's operating permissive, and external callers must not modify history entries.

| Input | `CUTTING_RUN` | `BOOL` | Actual cutting-equipment running status. |
| Input | `FaultTimestamp` | `DINT` | Current timestamp in seconds, used as the fault-record identifier. |
| Input | `CycleTime` | `TIME` | Actual elapsed interval represented by this invocation; must be positive. |
| Output | `THICKNESS_ALARM` | `BOOL` | Thickness alarm with a minimum 500 ms hold duration. |
| Output | `Slab_Fault_Counter` | `UINT` | Number of valid thickness-fault occurrences. |

# FIFO First-In-First-Out Queue

- **Difficulty:** Hard (hard)

## Requirements

Write a function block FB implementing a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) circular queue. Derive the queue capacity and element type from the caller-supplied buffer.

1. Each rising edge of enqueue requests one enqueue operation. If the queue is not full, append the current item value to its tail.
2. Each rising edge of dequeue requests one dequeue operation. If the queue is not empty, remove its front element and write that value back to item. The caller must not request enqueue and dequeue in the same invocation.
3. When reset is TRUE, empty the queue and set elementCount to zero. Reset takes priority over enqueue and dequeue; stored buffer values need not be overwritten.
4. Output the current number of valid elements through elementCount. Zero means the queue is empty; a count equal to the actual buffer array length means it is full.
5. Reject a dequeue request on an empty queue or an enqueue request on a full queue. Leave the queue and item unchanged and report the reason through status.
6. The queue is empty on its first invocation. Define head and tail positions and other internal state within the implementation; do not expose them as interface parameters.

Status codes:

- 16#0000: No error in this invocation, including idle, reset and successful operations.
- 16#8001: The dequeue request was rejected because the queue is empty.
- 16#8002: The enqueue request was rejected because the queue is full.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `enqueue` | `BOOL` | Enqueue request; one operation per rising edge. |
| Input | `dequeue` | `BOOL` | Dequeue request; one operation per rising edge. |
| Input | `reset` | `BOOL` | TRUE resets the queue to empty; takes priority over enqueue and dequeue. |
| Output | `elementCount` | `DINT` | Current number of valid elements, from zero through the queue capacity. |
| Output | `status` | `WORD` | Invocation status: 16#0000 no error, 16#8001 dequeue from an empty queue, 16#8002 enqueue into a full queue. |
| Input/Output | `item` | `VARIANT` | Mutable scalar reference: read its value when enqueuing; write the removed front value on successful dequeue. Its concrete type must match the array element type. |
| Input/Output | `buffer` | `VARIANT` | Reference to a nonempty one-dimensional array with a single concrete element type, used as queue storage. Capacity is the actual array length. |

Associate buffer with a nonempty, homogeneous one-dimensional array and item with a writable scalar of the same element type. Keep the buffer association fixed for each function-block instance. Derive capacity from the actual array length; it must fit in a positive DINT.

# Mechanical Arm Control - **Difficulty:** Hard (hard) ## Requirements Design a PLC program to control an automated mechanical arm that performs handling tasks on the production line. The mechanical arm has six basic actions: down, up, left, right, grip, and release. The operating modes of the mechanical arm include four types: manual, single step, single cycle, and continuous. Control requirements: 1. Manual mode: Allows the operator to control each action of the mechanical arm individually through the control panel, provided it is not yet in position. For example, pressing the down button (DownButton=1), if not at the down position (DownLimitSwitch=0), then move down (MoveDown=1); if at the down position (DownLimitSwitch=1), stop moving down. Releasing the down button also stops the movement down. 2. Single step mode: The mechanical arm automatically executes one action according to the preset program, and the operator needs to confirm after each action is completed to execute the next action. The initial position of the mechanical arm is at the top left. When the start button is pressed once, the mechanical arm executes the down command MoveDown, and stops after reaching the down position. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the grip command ActivateGrip, and stops after gripping. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the up command MoveUp, and stops after reaching the up position. When the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm executes the right command MoveRight, and stops after reaching the right position. When the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm executes the down command MoveDown, and stops after reaching the down position. When the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm executes the release command ActivateRelease, and stops after releasing. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the up command MoveUp, and stops after reaching the up position. When the start button is pressed again, the mechanical arm executes the left command MoveLeft, and stops after reaching the left position. Then starts the cycle again from the beginning 3. Single cycle mode: The mechanical arm automatically completes a full handling cycle, including all preset actions, and stops at the end of the cycle waiting for the operator's instruction. The initial position of the mechanical arm is at the top left, when the start button is pressed: The mechanical arm first moves down, then grips after reaching the down position, moves up after gripping, moves right after reaching the up position, moves down after reaching the right position, releases after reaching the down position, moves up after releasing, moves left after reaching the up position, and stops after reaching the left position. 4. Continuous mode: The initial position of the mechanical arm is at the top left, when the start button is pressed, the mechanical arm continuously executes the handling cycle of the single cycle mode. 5. The emergency stop function can stop all actions of the mechanical arm at any time. Use GripLimitSwitch and ReleaseLimitSwitch as the completion feedback for gripping and releasing respectively. # Production Control

- **Difficulty:** Hard (hard)

## Requirements

An automated production line consists of 5 workstations: material loading station, cleaning station, weighing station, firing station, and finished product station. The production line has a motor responsible for moving products from one workstation to the next, the sequence of the line is from the material loading station, cleaning station, weighing station, firing station, to the finished product station. Each workstation has a sensor (used to detect if the product has arrived).
Control requirements:
1. Mode Switching: The mode switch (Mode) is used to switch between manual and automatic modes of the production line. 0 = manual mode, 1 = automatic mode.
2. Manual Mode: In manual mode, the forward rotation button (ForwardButton) controls the forward rotation of the motor, and the reverse rotation button (ReverseButton) controls the reverse rotation of the motor. Forward and reverse rotation operations need to be interlocked and cannot be performed simultaneously.
3. Automatic Mode:
   - When the material arrives at the material loading station, the SensorFeed detects the material, the motor starts forward rotation, and moves the material to the cleaning station.
   - When the material arrives at the cleaning station, the SensorWash detects the material, the motor stops, and upon receiving the signal washComplete after cleaning is finished, the motor starts forward rotation, moving the material to the weighing station.
   - When the material arrives at the weighing station, the SensorWeight detects the material, the motor stops, and upon receiving weightComplete after weighing is complete, the material is judged to be qualified based on the weight value. If the weight value is greater than or equal to 100 and less than or equal to 200, it is qualified, otherwise not.
     If the material is unqualified, the rejection command kick is initiated.
     If the material is qualified, the firing temperature is calculated based on the weight value. The calculation rule is that the weight value from 100 to 200 linearly corresponds to the temperature value from 500 to 550. The firing temperature firingTemp is output. At the same time, the motor starts forward rotation, moving the material to the firing station.
   - When the product arrives at the firing station, the SensorFiring detects the material, the motor stops, and upon receiving the signal firingComplete after firing is finished, the motor starts forward rotation, moving the product to the finished product station.
   - When the product arrives at the finished product station, the SensorOutput detects the product, the motor stops, and the completion light (CompletionLight) turns on, indicating that the product processing is complete. When the product is taken away, i.e., the SensorOutput does not detect the product, the completion light (CompletionLight) turns off.

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `Mode` | `BOOL` | Used to switch the production line between manual and automatic modes, 0 = manual mode, 1 = automatic mode |

| Input | `ReverseButton` | `BOOL` | Reverse rotation button |
| Input | `SensorFeed` | `BOOL` | Sensor at the material loading station detecting the arrival of materials |
| Input | `SensorWash` | `BOOL` | Sensor at the cleaning station detecting the arrival of materials |
| Input | `SensorWeight` | `BOOL` | Sensor at the weighing station detecting the arrival of materials |
| Input | `SensorFiring` | `BOOL` | Sensor at the firing station detecting the arrival of materials |
| Input | `SensorOutput` | `BOOL` | Sensor at the finished product station detecting the arrival of products |

# Direction-biased elevator target selection

- **Difficulty:** Hard (hard)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_ElevatorTarget to select the next stopping floor of a six-floor elevator. Each call is one target-selection decision. The caller supplies CurrentFloor in 1..6 and Direction in {-1,0,1}, meaning down, idle and up.

2. CabReq and HallReq are read-only ARRAY[1..6] OF BOOL inputs. A floor i is eligible when CabReq[i] OR (HallReq[i] AND NOT FullLoad). The caller owns request registration and clearing. Never modify either request array.

3. If Enable is FALSE or no eligible request exists, set HasTarget=FALSE, TargetFloor=CurrentFloor and NextDirection=0. Otherwise, an eligible request at CurrentFloor takes priority: select it with HasTarget=TRUE and NextDirection=0.

4. For Direction=1, select the nearest eligible floor above CurrentFloor; if none exists above, select the nearest below. For Direction=-1, apply the mirrored rule. For Direction=0, select the nearest eligible floor on either side and break equal-distance ties toward the lower floor.

5. Set HasTarget=TRUE for a selected request. NextDirection is the sign of TargetFloor-CurrentFloor. Recompute outputs from the current inputs on every call, including the first call. Keep no internal request queue and issue no motor commands. FullLoad masks hall requests only; it must not erase them.

| Input | `Enable` | `BOOL` | Enable target selection. |

| Output | `TargetFloor` | `INT` | Selected floor, or CurrentFloor if no target. |

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_GateTelemetry for a remote water-gate telemetry station. FrameValid means that a complete frame passed lower-level validation and arrived during this call. FrameSeq is its UDINT sequence. Fresh is TRUE for a valid first frame or a valid frame whose sequence differs from the last accepted one. Compare inequality only: sequence wraparound is allowed, and replay authentication is outside scope.

2. At power-up or on Reset, clear frame history and set AgeMs=0, CommFault=TRUE, RemoteWritePermit=FALSE and Fresh=FALSE. Reset takes priority and ignores the other inputs for that scan. Remote writes start locked.

tasks.requirements:
# Winding diameter observer and speed compensation

- **Difficulty:** Hard (hard)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_RollGeometry using LREAL and PI=3.141592653589793. Fixed values are CoreD=76 mm, MaxD=140 mm and Thickness=0.135 mm. EncoderDelta is a DINT pulse increment in 0..1000000. A 50 mm diameter measuring roller produces 1024 pulses per revolution.

2. On the first legal call or when Reset=TRUE, initialize StoredLength=PI*(InitialD^2-CoreD^2)/(4*Thickness), Diameter=InitialD, MotorRPM=0 and LimitHit=FALSE. Ignore the pulse increment on this call. InitialD must be in [76,140] and is used only for initialization.

3. On other legal calls, deltaL=EncoderDelta*PI*50/1024. Add deltaL when Receiving=TRUE, otherwise subtract it. Clamp StoredLength to [0,Lmax], where Lmax=PI*(MaxD^2-CoreD^2)/(4*Thickness). Set LimitHit only when the unclamped value is strictly outside this interval; reaching a boundary exactly is not a limit hit.

4. Compute Diameter=SQRT(CoreD^2+4*Thickness*StoredLength/PI) from the updated length. Then compute MotorRPM=SpeedMpm*1000*50/(PI*Diameter) and clamp it to [-6000,6000]. SpeedMpm is signed line speed in [-15,15] m/min. Receiving determines material addition or removal independently of the speed sign.

5. Illegal SpeedMpm or EncoderDelta, or illegal InitialD when initializing, sets Error=TRUE, MotorRPM=0 and LimitHit=FALSE while preserving the length and diameter. Before successful initialization, hold StoredLength=0 and Diameter=76. A subsequent legal call may initialize. Legal calls clear Error. All real inputs are finite.

6. Assume constant thickness, tightly packed winding and no slip or elastic extension. Reset establishes a new geometric estimate; it does not represent material consumption. Absolute comparison tolerances are 0.001 mm for length and diameter, and 0.01 RPM for motor speed.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `Reset` | `BOOL` | Reinitialize the geometric estimate. |
| Input | `InitialD` | `LREAL` | Initial diameter, 76..140 mm; used only at initialization. |
| Input | `Receiving` | `BOOL` | TRUE adds wound material; FALSE removes it. |
| Input | `EncoderDelta` | `DINT` | Pulse increment in this call, 0..1000000. |
| Input | `SpeedMpm` | `LREAL` | Signed line speed, -15..15 m/min. |
| Output | `StoredLength` | `LREAL` | Material length outside the core, mm. |
| Output | `Diameter` | `LREAL` | Estimated diameter, mm; 76 before initialization. |
| Output | `MotorRPM` | `LREAL` | Motor speed setpoint, RPM. |
| Output | `LimitHit` | `BOOL` | The material-length update was strictly clipped. |
| Output | `Error` | `BOOL` | Illegal input. |

# Distance-triggered inspection imaging

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_InspectionCapture to trigger images at distance intervals along a rail-inspection run. DistanceMm is finite, nonnegative cumulative travel and is nondecreasing within a valid segment. SpacingMm is finite and positive when captured. Each segment spans at most 1e9 captured spacings, and the number of crossed sampling points is at most 1e9.

2. On the first call, Reset, or a FALSE-to-TRUE transition of Enable, capture DistanceMm as origin and latch SpacingMm. Clear CaptureCount, MissedCount and the internal crossed-point count; set CapturePulse=FALSE. Do not capture an image on the initialization scan. While disabled, emit no capture and retain counts; Reset may still establish a new segment.

3. During valid enabled operation, let k=FLOOR((DistanceMm-origin)/latched_spacing) and d=k-previous_crossed_count. If d=0, emit no capture. If d>0 and CameraBusy=FALSE, emit one current-scan CapturePulse, increment CaptureCount once and add d-1 to MissedCount. If busy, emit no capture and add d to MissedCount. Then update the crossed-point count to k.

4. Do not replay missed points after the camera becomes available: the vehicle is no longer at those locations. Spacing changes take effect only at Reset or segment re-enabling. The receiver consumes CapturePulse on every scan, not only on rising edges; consecutive crossing scans may both have CapturePulse=TRUE. CaptureCount counts issued requests, not confirmed image storage.

5. An invalid position, invalid initialization spacing, or a decrease below the last valid position latches Error=TRUE, suppresses captures and preserves counts and origin until a legal Reset or legal re-enable initialization. Continuous Reset rebuilds the origin each scan without capture. Counts start at zero.

| Input | `Enable` | `BOOL` | Segment enable; a rising edge establishes a new segment. |
| Input | `Reset` | `BOOL` | Reset the origin and counts. |
| Input | `DistanceMm` | `LREAL` | Nonnegative cumulative travel, mm. |
| Input | `SpacingMm` | `LREAL` | Positive spacing, mm, captured at segment initialization. |
| Input | `CameraBusy` | `BOOL` | Camera cannot accept a trigger in this scan. |
| Output | `CapturePulse` | `BOOL` | One image-capture request for this scan. |
| Output | `CaptureCount` | `UDINT` | Issued capture requests, not confirmed stored images. |
| Output | `MissedCount` | `UDINT` | Sampling points crossed without an issued request. |
| Output | `Error` | `BOOL` | Latched position/configuration error. |

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_CompressorPressure using LREAL. PressureKpa must be 0..1000 kPa, AirUseFlow 0..90 Nm3/min, Kp 0..1 percent/kPa, Ki 0..0.1 percent/(kPa*s), and DtSec 0.001..1 seconds. All real inputs are finite.

# Crane dual-drive speed consistency

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_CraneSpeedCheck to diagnose dual-drive speed consistency on a bridge crane. LeftSpeed10, RightSpeed10 and ReferenceSpeed10 are INT values in 0.1 RPM units, sampled by an upstream module in the same observation window. Only same-direction low-speed commissioning is in scope.

2. Inputs are valid when all three values are in 0..100 and ReferenceSpeed10>0. Otherwise set Invalid=TRUE and both other outputs FALSE. Validate ranges before subtraction and multiplication; do not perform unchecked INT arithmetic on extreme input values. Promoting to DINT is allowed.

3. The benchmark specifies equal left/right speeds and a target speed on each side equal to 6.5 times the reference reduction shaft speed. For valid inputs, SyncOK is TRUE exactly when ABS(LeftSpeed10-RightSpeed10)<=1 AND ABS(LeftSpeed10+RightSpeed10-13*ReferenceSpeed10)<=2. Otherwise set SyncBad=TRUE.

4. Recompute outputs independently every scan. Initially all three outputs are FALSE; after each call exactly one is TRUE. Both constraints must be checked; averaging the two sides must not replace the synchronization check. Ratios, ranges and tolerances are synthetic benchmark values, not crane nameplate data. Do not command crane motion.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `LeftSpeed10` | `INT` | Left-side speed in 0.1 RPM units. |
| Input | `RightSpeed10` | `INT` | Right-side speed in 0.1 RPM units. |
| Input | `ReferenceSpeed10` | `INT` | Reference reduction-shaft speed in 0.1 RPM units. |
| Output | `SyncOK` | `BOOL` | Both synchronization and gearing constraints hold. |
| Output | `SyncBad` | `BOOL` | Inputs valid but at least one constraint fails. |
| Output | `Invalid` | `BOOL` | Any channel out of range or reference speed zero. |

# Spectrometer recalibration after maintenance

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_SpectrometerQualification for measurement eligibility after maintenance of an online spectrometer. State 0 means waiting for calibration, 1 ready and 2 maintenance. Initially State=0, CalibReq=TRUE, MaintLamp=FALSE and MeasurePermit=FALSE.

2. Maintenance=TRUE has priority and moves every state to 2. With Maintenance=FALSE, a pre-scan State of 2 must first move to 0, even if CalibDone=TRUE on the same call. A pre-scan State of 0 moves to 1 only when CalibDone=TRUE, otherwise remains 0. State 1 remains ready while not in maintenance.

3. Perform at most one transition per call, using the pre-scan state. CalibReq is TRUE exactly when the updated State is 0; MaintLamp exactly when it is 2. MeasurePermit equals the current MeasureReq AND updated State=1.

4. CalibDone is a completion level supplied by an external calibration module. No fresh edge is required; the specific constraint is that the maintenance-exit scan cannot skip state 0. Spectral fitting, calibration computation and physical measurement are outside scope.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `Maintenance` | `BOOL` | Maintenance mode. |
| Input | `CalibDone` | `BOOL` | External calibration-complete level. |
| Input | `MeasureReq` | `BOOL` | Measurement request. |
| Output | `State` | `USINT` | 0 waiting for calibration, 1 ready, 2 maintenance. |
| Output | `CalibReq` | `BOOL` | Request the upstream calibration module. |
| Output | `MaintLamp` | `BOOL` | Maintenance indication. |
| Output | `MeasurePermit` | `BOOL` | Ordinary measurement eligibility. |

# Deferred warehouse inventory request lifecycle

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_InventoryRequest for one pending warehouse-inventory service request, not a multi-item queue. Initially Pending, RequestLamp, Dispatched and internal PrevCall are FALSE. Update the previous RequestBtn value every scan, including cancellation scans.

2. Cancel=TRUE has highest priority: clear Pending and Dispatched, but still update button history. Otherwise a rising RequestBtn creates a request. Let Request=previous_Pending OR current_button_rise.

3. If Request AND ServiceReady AND NOT Busy, set Dispatched=TRUE and Pending=FALSE for this scan. Otherwise set Dispatched=FALSE and preserve an unconsumed request in Pending. Busy must not lose a request, even when ServiceReady=TRUE. RequestLamp always equals Pending.

4. A held button must not register repeatedly. A button held across cancellation release must not create a new request. A new request may be dispatched immediately when service is available in the same scan. Dispatched means a task was issued, not that physical inventory work was completed.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `RequestBtn` | `BOOL` | Inventory-request button; rising-edge registration. |
| Input | `ServiceReady` | `BOOL` | Inventory service can receive a task. |
| Input | `Busy` | `BOOL` | Inventory resource is busy. |
| Input | `Cancel` | `BOOL` | Cancel the pending request; highest priority. |

# Vehicle weighbridge redundant-channel voting

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_WeighbridgeVote. LoadA, LoadB and LoadC are DINT measurements of the same whole-vehicle mass from three independent channels, not three support forces to be summed. Each channel is valid in 0..20000 kg. ReleaseReq and BarrierReady are BOOL. Validate ranges before computing differences with sufficiently wide arithmetic.

2. Consider pairs (A,B), (A,C) and (B,C). A pair is consistent when both channels are valid and its absolute difference is <=200 kg. Select the consistent pair with minimum difference; break ties in order AB, AC, BC. Even with three valid channels, do not simply average all three. PairMask is 3 for AB, 5 for AC and 6 for BC.

3. VotedKg is the LREAL arithmetic mean of the chosen two measurements and may contain 0.5 kg. With no consistent pair, set PairMask=0, VotedKg=0, LoadFault=TRUE, Overload=FALSE and ReleasePermit=FALSE.

4. With a consistent pair, set LoadFault=FALSE and Overload exactly when VotedKg>10000. ReleasePermit equals ReleaseReq AND BarrierReady AND NOT Overload. Request or barrier readiness only affects permission and must not change the voting result.

5. Recompute independently on every scan with no retained voting state. Initially PairMask=0, VotedKg=0 and all flags FALSE; apply the rules on the first call. The range, capacity threshold and consistency window are synthetic benchmark settings, not metrology certification limits. Absolute numeric tolerance is 1e-6.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `LoadA` | `DINT` | Independent whole-vehicle mass A, 0..20000 kg. |
| Input | `LoadB` | `DINT` | Independent whole-vehicle mass B, 0..20000 kg. |
| Input | `LoadC` | `DINT` | Independent whole-vehicle mass C, 0..20000 kg. |
| Input | `ReleaseReq` | `BOOL` | Release request. |
| Input | `BarrierReady` | `BOOL` | Barrier-control readiness condition. |
| Output | `PairMask` | `USINT` | 0 no pair, 3 AB, 5 AC, 6 BC. |
| Output | `VotedKg` | `LREAL` | Fused whole-vehicle mass, kg. |
| Output | `LoadFault` | `BOOL` | No valid consistent measurement pair. |
| Output | `Overload` | `BOOL` | Fused mass strictly above 10000 kg. |
| Output | `ReleasePermit` | `BOOL` | Ordinary benchmark release condition. |

# Marine buoy budget-constrained auxiliary loads

- **Difficulty:** Medium (medium)

## Requirements

1. Implement FB_BuoyPowerBudget for a battery-powered marine monitoring buoy. Three loads are sensor unit SensorOn, instrument anti-freeze heater HeaterOn and radio RadioOn, represented by mask bits 1,2,4. Their fixed powers are respectively 40,70,60 W and utility scores 7,10,9. These are benchmark settings. NeedSensor, NeedHeater and NeedRadio are current requests.

2. Enable=FALSE has priority and sets all outputs to zero/FALSE. Otherwise BudgetW is valid in 0..200 W. An invalid budget sets Error=TRUE and all other outputs to zero/FALSE. Legal operation sets Error=FALSE.

3. MandatorySensor=TRUE requires the sensor unit even if NeedSensor=FALSE. Other unrequested loads may not be selected. With MandatorySensor=FALSE, the sensor unit is eligible only when requested; all requested loads may be shed to meet the budget.

4. If MandatorySensor=TRUE but BudgetW<40, set BudgetShortage=TRUE, turn off all loads and set SelectedMask=PowerW=Score=0. Never exceed budget to force the mandatory load on. All other legal situations have BudgetShortage=FALSE.

5. Enumerate all subsets of eligible loads whose total power is <=BudgetW and that satisfy the mandatory-sensor constraint. First maximize total Score, then minimize total PowerW, then select the numerically smallest SelectedMask. The empty subset is allowed; with no requests and no mandatory load select it.

6. The three Boolean outputs must match SelectedMask; PowerW and Score are sums for that subset. Recompute independently each scan; all outputs initially equal zero/FALSE. Greedy selection by individual score or score/power ratio must not replace the global optimum. Battery state of charge, sea conditions and physical temperature are outside scope.

## Interface Definition

| Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `Enable` | `BOOL` | Enable budget optimization. |
| Input | `BudgetW` | `UINT` | Available power, 0..200 W. |
| Input | `NeedSensor` | `BOOL` | Sensor-unit request. |
| Input | `NeedHeater` | `BOOL` | Instrument-heater request. |
| Input | `NeedRadio` | `BOOL` | Radio request. |
| Input | `MandatorySensor` | `BOOL` | Require the sensor unit. |
| Output | `SelectedMask` | `USINT` | Selected subset mask, bits 1,2,4. |
| Output | `SensorOn` | `BOOL` | Sensor-unit setpoint. |
| Output | `HeaterOn` | `BOOL` | Instrument-heater setpoint. |
| Output | `RadioOn` | `BOOL` | Radio setpoint. |
| Output | `PowerW` | `UINT` | Total selected power, W. |
| Output | `Score` | `USINT` | Total selected utility. |
| Output | `BudgetShortage` | `BOOL` | The mandatory sensor cannot be powered. |
| Output | `Error` | `BOOL` | Illegal budget. |

V := 0<=BudgetW<=200；B := MandatorySensor AND BudgetW<40。

对m=0..7，p(m)=40*[m&1!=0]+70*[m&2!=0]+60*[m&4!=0]；s(m)=7*[m&1!=0]+10*[m&2!=0]+9*[m&4!=0]。
feasible(m) := (m无A以外的比特) AND p(m)<=BudgetW AND (!MandatorySensor OR m&1!=0)。

disabled := !Enable；invalid := Enable AND !V；shortage := Enable AND V AND B；normal := Enable AND V AND !B。

maskMapOK表示SensorOn、HeaterOn、RadioOn与SelectedMask比特1/2/4逐一等价。
